Result views, connections and pooling in dsOMOPClient

Source: R/conventions.R
dsomop_conventions.Rd

dsOMOPClient follows the dsBaseClient conventions for every function that contacts the servers.

Connections

datasources names the DataSHIELD connections to use. NULL (the default) uses the connections stored in the OMOP session of symbol when one exists, and otherwise DSI::datashield.connections_find(). The older name conns keeps working (with a one-time message); giving both with different connections is an error.

Result views (type)

  • "split": the per-server results only ($per_site).

  • "combine": the pooled result only ($pooled). When the result cannot be pooled, the call stops with the reason, before contacting the servers when the reason is known in advance.

  • "both": both. When pooling is impossible the per-server results are kept, $pooled is NULL and meta$pooling_reason says why.

Count and table readers (ds.omop.table.stats, ds.omop.domain.coverage, ds.omop.date.counts, ds.omop.value.counts, ds.omop.crosstab, ds.omop.concept.locate, ds.omop.achilles.results) default to "both", as ds.dim, ds.length and ds.table do. Readers of means and distributions default to "split", as ds.mean and ds.var do. Aliases: "s", "splits", "per_site" (split); "c", "combined" (combine); "b", "pooled" (both). The older scope ("per_site", "pooled") and pool (FALSE, TRUE) arguments keep working as aliases of "split" and "both".

Every pooled result records how it was pooled in meta$pooling (method and estimand). Pooled counts are sums of the servers' banded counts: a person present in several databases counts once per database.

Pooling policy

pooling_policy = "strict" (the default) releases a pooled value only when every server returned it: a group (value, concept, period, bin, cell) absent or suppressed on any server is left out or NA, and an unavailable server leaves the whole pooled result NULL. "pooled_only_ok" pools the servers that did return a disclosure-safe value, so a pooled value may cover only some servers; the warnings name what was left out. Suppressed contributions are never treated as zero under either policy.

Output names

Functions that create one server-side object accept newobj for its name, as dsBaseClient assigning functions do.
